```yaml
gates:
  required:
    - "ruby MASTER/tools/convergence/evidence_gate.rb"
    - "ruby DEPLOY/rails/archive_restore_gate.rb"
    - "ruby DEPLOY/rails/check_production_gate.rb"
```

### MASTER/data/limits.yml

```yaml
# MASTER limits — operational principles, pipeline budgets, and workflow rules.
# Governs how MASTER and its LLM agents read, edit, scan, and fix code.

schema: 1
file_reading:
  rule: READ_FULL_FILES
  statement: "Read complete files. Never grep, head, tail, or partial‑read to understand code."
  rationale: "Partial view yields partial (wrong) changes."
  allowed_exceptions:
    - "grep/search across many unknown files to locate a keyword"
  forbidden:
    - "grep pattern file to understand code structure"
    - "head -N file to check structure"
    - "tail -N file to check endings"

before_edit:
  rule: READ_BEFORE_WRITE
  statement: "Read every file that could be affected before editing any file."
  see_also: edit_context
  steps:
    - "Map the codebase: find all .rb files in lib/"
    - "Trace callers before changing any public method signature"
    - "Check Zeitwerk inflectors before renaming classes or files"
    - "Run ruby -c FILE after every write"
    - "Run ruby -e require_relative after every commit"

edit_context:
  rule: TIERED_BLAST_RADIUS_READ
  statement: "Read depth scales with change radius — not every edit requires a full-corpus read."
  always:
    - "Full read of every file you will edit"
    - "Re-read from disk immediately before writing"
    - "One-hop callers/tests for any public method or constant you change"
  tiers:
    local_fix:
      when: "single-file bugfix or comment; no signature change"
      read: ["target file", "matching test file", "direct callers"]
    module_change:
      when: "new class, renamed constant, or cross-file behavior in one lib/ module"
      read: ["module entrypoint", "/graph one-hop dependents", "affected tests"]
    structural_change:
      when: "pipeline stage, scan rule, constitution data, or DEPLOY topology"
      read: ["data/soul.yml ABSOLUTE sections", "limits.yml scan_profiles", "/scan deep on affected tree"]
  forbidden:
    - "Edit from grep snippets, partial reads, or conversation memory"
    - "Claim a fix without reading the file being changed"
  note: "Pairs with llm_ergonomics — external grep/rg for reconnaissance is allowed; production edits require full-file reads."

code_principles:
  no_hardcoding:
    rule: NO_HARDCODED_CONSTANTS
    statement: "Prose, patterns, and config belong in data/*.yml, not Ruby strings."
  single_source:
    rule: ONE_SOURCE
    statement: "If it is in a data file, the code reads from there. No duplicates."
  no_magic_numbers:
    rule: NAMED_CONSTANTS
    statement: "Extract literals to named constants with .freeze"
  no_bare_rescue:
    rule: SPECIFIC_RESCUE
    statement: "Always rescue SpecificError => e. Propagate or log via event bus."
  guard_first:
    rule: GUARD_CLAUSES_FIRST
    statement: "Return Result.ok(ctx) unless condition before main logic."
  one_responsibility:
    rule: SINGLE_RESPONSIBILITY
    statement: "Split if you can name two reasons to change it."
  cqs:
    rule: COMMAND_QUERY_SEPARATION
    statement: "Queries return data and do not mutate. Commands mutate and do not return values."
  inject_deps:
    rule: DEPENDENCY_INJECTION
    statement: "Never instantiate collaborators inside a method."
  result_monad:
    rule: RESULT_MONAD
    statement: "Pipeline stages return Master::Result. Use .ok? and .err?; propagate Err without calling .value!."

scan_rules:
  note: "DEEP_SCAN_ONLY — every scan runs at deep depth. scan_profiles (cosmetic, core, …) filter the report after the scan; they are not depth tiers."
  standard_depth:
    - frozen_string
    - bare_rescue
    - explicit
    - immutable
    - cqs
    - self_explaining
    - long_method
    - god_class
    - duplicate_code
    - prune
    - srp
    - pola
    - nielsen
  deep_only:
    - semantic
    - adversarial
  hunt_only:
    - rubocop
    - reek
  notes:
    nielsen: "puts is NOT debug output in a CLI. Only p, pp, binding.pry, debugger are."
    prune: "Loads patterns from data/voice.yml (voice.strunk); legacy fallback in rules.yml."
    semantic: "Loads detect_semantic prompts from data/rules.yml scan corpus."
    deep_caution: "deep adds 2 LLM calls per file. With 90 files at 8 req/min free tier = 22+ minutes."

principle_groups:
  axioms:      [frozen_string, explicit, immutable, self_explaining]
  solid:       [srp, cqs, pola]
  solid_focus: [srp, cqs, pola, frozen_string, explicit, immutable, self_explaining]
  coding:      [explicit, immutable, cqs, frozen_string, bare_rescue]
  clean_code:  [long_method, god_class, duplicate_code, bare_rescue]
  ui:          [nielsen, prune]
  llm:         [semantic, adversarial]
  operations:  [bare_rescue, explicit, immutable]
  design:      [srp, cqs, pola, prune]
  architecture: [god_class, duplicate_code, srp, cqs]
  interface:   [nielsen, prune]
  llm_rules:   [semantic, adversarial]
  heavy:       [rubocop, reek]
  core:        [frozen_string, bare_rescue, explicit, long_method, god_class]
  critical:    [frozen_string, bare_rescue, explicit, immutable, srp, cqs]
  cosmetic:
    - TRAILING_WHITESPACE
    - CONSECUTIVE_BLANK_LINES
    - NO_COLUMN_ALIGN
    - TRAILING_COMMENT
    - TAB_CHARACTER
    - FINAL_NEWLINE
    - TYPOGRAPHIC_EXCELLENCE
    - TYPOGRAPHY_DISCIPLINE
    - NO_ASCII_LINE_ART
    - RUBY_SNAKE_METHODS
    - RUBY_CAMEL_CLASS
    - RUBY_NUMERIC_UNDERSCORE
    - RUBY_SYMBOL_TO_PROC
    - RUBY_BLOCK_DELIMITER
    - RUBY_TERNARY_NOT_NESTED
    - NO_ABBREVIATED_IDENTIFIERS
    - DOUBLE_QUOTES_RUBY
    - EN_DASH_RANGE
    - MEASURE_OPTIMUM
    - ALL_CAPS_NO_TRACKING
    - TRAILING_COMMAS
    - MEANINGFUL_NAMES
    - USE_THEN
    - RESCUE_ON_DEF
    - MAGIC_COLOR
    - NO_LONG_TRANSITION
    - LONG_LINE

scan_profiles:
  default: full
  core:
    rules: core
    aliases: [quick]
    description: "Core axiom and small-function findings after a deep scan"
  full:
    rules: "*"
    aliases: [all]
    description: "All registered scan rules"
  axioms_only:
    rules: axioms
    aliases: [axioms]
    description: "Constitutional axioms only"
  solid_focus:
    rules: solid_focus
    aliases: [solid]
    description: "SOLID principles plus axioms"
  critical:
    rules: "*"
    severity: [error, veto]
    description: "Only error and veto findings for urgent triage"
  solid:
    rules: solid_focus
    description: "SOLID principles focus"
  axioms:
    rules: axioms
    description: "Constitutional axioms only"
  cosmetic:
    rules: cosmetic
    aliases: [style, hygiene, perfection]
    description: "Hygiene, micro-typography, naming, and style-perfection lint"

conflicts:
  strategy: highest_priority_wins
  rules:
    - condition: "dry conflicts with wet or aha"
      resolution: "favor wet/aha if fewer than 3 duplications exist"
    - condition: "clarity conflicts with simplicity"
      resolution: "favor clarity"
    - condition: "fix introduces higher priority violation"
      resolution: "reject fix, report to autoloop"

frontend_protection:
  statement: "Only application.scss is protected — one entry per app; reuse pub4_stack and existing partials (brgen-style) before adding files."
  protected_files:
    - application.scss
  on_view_or_css_edit:
    - flatten divitis and use semantic landmarks
    - bare tag targeting per style.yml — no BEM or utility soup in ERB
    - run Shared::FrontendAuditor on touched paths
  mailer_exempt:
    - inline styles in mailer views (email clients require them)

universal_scope:
  policy: ALL_PRINCIPLES_ALL_FILES
  statement: >
    All axioms, principles, and philosophies apply to every file in the codebase
    regardless of file type: Ruby, YAML, Zsh, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Markdown.
    Language-specific rules apply only to their target language; universal rules
    (SQUINT_TEST, TYPOGRAPHY_DISCIPLINE, MEANINGFUL_NAMES, etc.) apply everywhere.
  scan_glob: "**/*.{rb,rake,erb,html,htm,css,scss,js,ts,jsx,tsx,zsh,sh,yml,yaml,md}"
  semantic_rules: all_known_languages
  adversarial_rules: all_known_languages

incremental_scanning:
  enabled: true
  strategy: modified_files_only
  triggers:
    full_scan:
      - new_principle_added
      - master_yml_modified
      - user_requests_full_scan
    incremental:
      - file_saved
      - git_stage
      - git_commit
  speedup_estimate: "60-85% fewer files on typical edit"
  fallback: full_scan_on_error

autoloop:
  background: true
  startup_delay: 90
  idle_sleep: 300
  scan_depth: deep
  scan_nice: 15
  scan_file_sleep_s: 2
  fix_depth: llm
  batch_size: 1
  max_cycles: 12
  rate_limit_sleep: 30
  max_file_bytes: 16000
  max_fix_retries: 3
  confidence_threshold: 0.60
  targets:
    - lib/
    - test/
    - data/
    - web/
    - DEPLOY/
  excludes:
    - vendor/
    - knowledge/
    - fix_
    - patch_

sweep:
  scan_depth: deep
  converge_threshold: 0.05
  converge_window: 2
  max_cycles: 16
  codebase_map: true

zeitwerk:
  inflections:
    autoloop: AutoLoop
    cli: CLI
    mcp_server: MCPServer
    mcp_coordinator: McpCoordinator
    diff_stager: DiffStager
    code_index: CodeIndex
    git_context: GitContext
    ast_edit: AstEdit
    llm: LLM

anti_sprawl:
  mode: aggressive
  hierarchy: openbsd_ruby_roda
  max_lib_depth: 4
  fold_suffixes: [_support, _helper, _util, _helpers, _utils]
  forbidden_files:
    - summary.md
    - analysis.md
    - report.md
    - todo.md
    - notes.md
    - changelog.md
  slug_naming: "Rails-parameterized density — snake_case, concrete tokens only, Strunk-clean; see style.yml naming.paths"
  rule: "Flat Hierarchy — merge thin siblings and rename misfit paths before creating files. OpenBSD-flat paths, Zeitwerk-true dense slugs, Roda-tight trees."

validation:
  after_write: "ruby -c lib/FILE.rb"
  after_commit: "ruby -e \"require_relative 'lib/master'; puts 'ok'\""
  scan_file: "bundle exec ruby bin/cli scan lib/FILE.rb"

phases:
  discover:
    id: 1
    goal: "Understand actual need"
    output: "Problem statement with success criteria"
    personas: [chaos, user]
    introspect: "What assumptions did we make?"
    gates:
      - no_vague_words
      - audience_identified
      - success_measurable
  analyze:
    id: 2
    goal: "Break into components"
    output: "Component diagram with dependencies"
    personas: [skeptic, maintainer]
    introspect: "What did we miss?"
    gates:
      - components_distinct
      - dependencies_acyclic
  ideate:
    id: 3
    goal: "Generate 15+ alternatives"
    output: "List of approaches with trade‑offs"
    personas: [minimalist, chaos]
    introspect: "Which ideas surprised us?"
    gates:
      - count_gte_15
      - trade_offs_documented
  design:
    id: 4
    goal: "Specific architecture"
    output: "Interface definitions and error handling"
    personas: [security, accessibility]
    introspect: "What could break?"
    gates:
      - interfaces_explicit
      - errors_documented
  implement:
    id: 5
    goal: "Execute with zero violations"
    output: "Working code at 100/100 score"
    personas: [performance, security]
    introspect: "Is this the simplest solution?"
    gates:
      - tests_pass
      - zero_violations
  validate:
    id: 6
    goal: "Prove with evidence"
    output: "Test results, benchmarks"
    personas: [skeptic, security]
    introspect: "What evidence proves it works?"
    gates:
      - zero_test_failures
      - edge_cases_covered
  deliver:
    id: 7
    goal: "Ship with monitoring"
    output: "Deployed code with dashboards"
    personas: [realist]
    introspect: "What would the user complain about?"
    gates:
      - deployed
      - monitoring_configured
  learn:
    id: 8
    goal: "Extract durable lessons"
    output: "Updated defaults, new memory entries, refined rules"
    personas: [skeptic, chaos]
    introspect: "What would we do differently next time?"
    gates:
      - lessons_captured
      - defaults_updated
session_startup:
  reading_tiers:
    explore:
      required: [/orient bootstrap]
      optional: [data/soul.yml ABSOLUTE sections]
      note: "Recon and analysis — pair with llm_ergonomics; external rg allowed."
    structural_edit:
      required: [data/soul.yml, data/rules.yml, data/limits.yml]
      optional: [data/voice.yml, data/style.yml, data/state.yml]
      note: "Before production edits and deploy-touching changes."
    production_ops:
      required: [data/operator_playbook.yml]
      optional: [/orient trace]
      note: "VPS friction, relayd, recovery — run bin/playbook when signals match."
  mandatory_reads:
    - "See reading_tiers — /orient bootstrap first; full constitution only for structural edits."
  playbook_command: "bin/playbook — print codified operator lessons when signals match production friction"
  check_standing_orders: "Verify FSM state before any mutation -- UNCHANGE blocks refactoring"
  scan_before_analysis: "Use /scan deep via MASTER, not external agents, for code analysis"
  ssh_edit_pattern: "Write to /tmp, run ruby /tmp/patch.rb -- never ruby -i with heredoc"

corruption_prevention:
  llm_error_in_file: "git checkout HEAD -- data/ && rcctl restart master -- LLM error strings silently overwrite YAML data files when circuit is open and agent#ask returns error string instead of raising"
  sweep_excludes_data: "Sweep may scan data/*.yml but must not LLM-rewrite them. Structural violations (duplicate keys, bad indentation) are auto-fixed. Exclude .master/ runtime state files entirely."
  yaml_type_guards: "All load_yaml calls must type-check result before use (is_a?(Array/Hash)) -- circuit-open strings parse as valid YAML scalars"
  ask_raises_on_error: "agent#ask must raise StandardError when result.err? -- callers must rescue, never silently propagate error strings as LLM output"

# Phase-appropriate quality gates — prototype is permissive, production is strict.
# Source: master.json v225 reunification.
quality_phases:
  prototype:
    gates:           [functional]
    debt_allowed:    high
    speed:           maximize
  production:
    gates:           [functional, secure, maintainable, performant]
    debt_allowed:    none
    speed:           sustainable
  legacy:
    gates:           [functional, secure]
    changes:         surgical_only
    risk_tolerance:  minimal

# Conflicts already declared above; add reinforcements that multiply effectiveness.
# Source: master.json v225 reunification.
principle_reinforcements:
  dry_and_kiss:               multiply_effectiveness
  evidence_and_reversible:    enables_confident_change
  single_responsibility_and_dependency_injection: enables_isolated_testing

# Observability spec — structured logging, levels, exported metrics.
# Source: master.json v225 reunification.
observability:
  logging:
    format:    json
    fields:    [timestamp, level, phase, file, evidence_score, decision]
    levels:
      trace:  every_operation
      debug:  decision_points
      info:   phase_transitions
      warn:   evidence_below_threshold
      error:  gate_failures
  metrics:
    track:             [evidence_score, complexity, coverage, churn, council_consensus]
    export_format:     prometheus
    threshold_alerts:  true

# Adaptive file-processing strategy by size. Replaces hard MAX_FILE_BYTES cutoff.
# Source: master.json v225 reunification.
processing_strategies:
  small_file:
    condition: "size <= 10240"
    method:    full_read
    context:   entire_file
  medium_file:
    condition: "10240 < size <= 1048576"
    method:    streaming
    context:   line_by_line_with_lookahead
  large_file:
    condition: "size > 1048576"
    method:    chunked
    context:   section_by_section
    checkpoint: per_chunk

# Cap on tool calls per turn before MASTER pauses for self-reflection.
# Source: Augment reunification (#68, #69).
tool_budget:
  max_calls_per_turn:        40
  max_consecutive_edits:      8     # forces a read-back after N edits
  max_consecutive_searches:  10
  on_exceed: "publish budget:exceeded; force /reflect before next call"

# Principle pairs that pull in opposite directions; declare resolution.
# Source: master.json v225 reunification (#54).
antagonisms:
  minimalism_vs_explicit:        "explicit wins for safety-critical paths"
  speed_vs_evidence:             "evidence wins always"
  abstraction_vs_proximity:      "proximity wins below 3 occurrences"
  dry_vs_singularity:            "singularity wins for data, dry wins for code"
  completeness_vs_density:       "density wins; defer completeness to next iteration"

# Save LLM calls — only run round 2 if round 1 dissent exceeds threshold.
# Source: master.yml v31 reunification (#61).
two_stage_council:
  round_one:    "each persona votes ack/dissent independently, no debate"
  dissent_threshold: 0.30   # fraction of weighted disagreement triggering round 2
  round_two:    "only dissenting personas debate, others abstain"
  saves: "60-80% of LLM calls when consensus is clear"

# Long tasks surface a navigable thread of decisions.
# Source: Amp reunification (#70).
view_thread:
  emit_event: "thread:decision"
  fields:     [timestamp, phase, file, decision, alternatives_considered, rationale]
  persist_to: "data/threads/${session_id}.jsonl"
  rotate_after_days: 7

# Auto-compact context every N turns. Pairs with data/compression.yml.
# Source: Cline reunification (#77).
checkpoint_summarization:
  every_n_turns:           5
  every_n_tokens:    100_000
  keep_verbatim:           ["last_3_user_messages", "current_violation_set", "current_diff"]
  summarize:               ["all_other_turns"]
  target_compression:      0.30   # aim for 30% of original

# LLM Ergonomics — explicit guidance for working with current-generation models.
# Added to reduce friction for future agents while preserving constitutional integrity.
# Source: 2026 reassessment of agent experience.
llm_ergonomics:
  core_principle: "Optimize for actual LLM behavior and context limits, not idealized super-agents."
  guidance:
    - "Provide high-density mental models (/orient bootstrap) before requiring deep constitution reads."
    - "Allow external tools (grep, rg, find) for reconnaissance and understanding. Require constitutional tools only for production changes."
    - "When full strict adherence would cause context exhaustion or paralysis, prefer 'good enough + evidence' over perfect ceremony."
    - "Document known friction points openly so future agents can work around them intelligently."
    - "Event emission should be rich and first-class by default so observers (human or visual) can understand internal state without heroic effort."
  tension_with_rules: "This section provides pragmatic guidance for working with real LLM limitations. It does not override any ABSOLUTE rules defined in soul.yml."

# Spec arrives -> code streams in parallel where safe.
# Source: Bolt reunification (#78).
spec_streaming:
  triggers:    ["new_module_creation", "stub_to_implementation"]
  safe_for:    ["non-overlapping files", "additive_changes"]
  forbidden_for: ["mutating_shared_state", "schema_migrations"]

# UI changes must render before commit. Closes the visual-regression gap.
# Source: Lovable reunification (#79).
live_preview_gate:
  triggers:    ["edit under web/app/views/", "edit under web/app/assets/"]
  require:     "successful render at preview URL within 10s"
  on_failure:  "block commit; publish preview:render_failed"

# Feed MASTER its own commits and ask: would you approve these now?
# Source: cross-cutting reunification (#90).
reverse_introspection:
  cadence:        "after_every_10_commits"
  sample_size:    5
  on_disapproval: "open issue tagged self_review with proposed reversion"

# For each scan rule, auto-generate test cases proving it fires/passes correctly.
# Source: cross-cutting reunification (#94).
test_generation:
  target_dir:   "test/rules_generated/"
  cadence:      "on_rule_definition_change"
  coverage_required: 0.80

# Self-rewrite throttle — sensitive paths require explicit user approval.
# Source: cross-cutting reunification (#100).
self_rewrite_throttle:
  sensitive_paths:
    - lib/loop/
    - lib/ground/
    - lib/judge/security/
    - bin/cli
    - data/state.yml
  autoloop_action: "skip with publish autoloop:throttled event; surface to user"

# Adversarial questioning — every scan, sweep, and council turn asks these.
# Trivial findings get autofixed immediately. Non-trivial findings get N options
# proposed, from which the best is cherry-picked by the operator or judge.
adversarial_questioning:
  mandate: fires_on_every_scan_and_council_turn
  questions:
    - "What is wrong with this design that I have not spotted?"
    - "What would an attacker do with this code?"
    - "What assumption is this built on that could be false?"
    - "What breaks at scale or under failure?"
    - "Is this wired to anything? Could it be deleted without loss?"
    - "Is there a simpler approach that was not taken?"
    - "What should be relocated or transformed to a different format?"
  resolution:
    trivial: autofix immediately — no proposal, no prompt
    non_trivial: "propose 3 concrete options (OPTION 1/2/3 + RECOMMEND), await cherry-pick"
    threshold: "non-trivial if the fix spans more than one file, touches architecture, or has security implications"

# Known issues — active bugs and watch-outs from operator_playbook.yml.
known_issues:
  relayd_master_empty: "After rcctl restart master, relayd may mark master empty until /up health passes — tracked rc.d waits for local /up then restarts relayd; relayd.conf must use check http \"/up\" not \"/\" for master."
  relayd_stale_backend_tables: "After mass app restarts relayctl may show empty/down while local /up is 200 — relayd-watchdog (cron */5) restarts relayd when backends are live but tables are stale."
  resource_guard_shedding: "DEPLOY/openbsd/resource_guard.sh stops optional Rails apps when load/mem thresholds hit unless /var/db/pub4_all_apps exists — use start_all_apps.sh to pin."
  rails_phantom_fk: "references with foreign_key: true alone creates phantom buyers/listings/likers/orders tables on SQLite — always set to_table. Run ruby DEPLOY/rails/check_phantom_foreign_keys.rb."
  todo_checkbox_drift: "Retired 2026-06-24 — verify ship readiness with bin/probe repo, health_check.rb, and per-app bin/ci instead of checkbox backlogs."
  tts_broken: "Master::Voice::Speech.synthesize_bytes shells to bin/tts-worker; if edge-tts is missing or tts-worker crashes, speech silently falls back to espeak. Verify bin/tts-worker exists and edge-tts is installed (pkg_add py3-edge-tts or pip)."
  particle_swarm: "Fixed 2026-06-24 — ecology canvas was z-index 0 under face (z-index 1); now z-index 2 with screen blend. verify trails/weather visible over face after SSE events."
  gemfile_separation: "MASTER/Gemfile and MASTER/web/Gemfile are independent. Any gem used by lib/ code that is also called from web/ controllers must appear in both. Adding to one only causes LoadError in the other context."
  tts_worker_process: "Process.fork inside a Falcon fiber raises 'Closing scheduler' — EM-based gems and subprocess-heavy tools must use Open3.popen or shell out via exe/<name>-worker, never fork."
```

### MASTER/data/llm_operators.yml

```yaml
# LLM operator prompts — how to get real work out of each model.
# Used by MASTER when routing tasks. Keyed by model family.
# Each entry: reading_gate, context_format, output_format, strengths, traps.
#
# Reading gate = the verification step that proves the model read the code
# before it acts. Skip it and you get pattern-matched hallucination.

operators:

  grok:
    aliases: [grok-4.3, grok-4.20, x-ai/grok-4-fast, x-ai/grok-4]
    context_window: "1M (4.3) / 2M (4.20)"
    strengths:
      - Fast iteration and prototyping
      - Real-time web context via browse_page + web_search
      - Persistent bash shell (30s default, up to 600s) — can grep/cat to verify
      - Aggressive at producing runnable code quickly
      - Mirrors user's dialect, language, and alphabet exactly
      - Independent analysis on contentious topics; does not defer to xAI or past responses
    traps:
      - System prompt has NO built-in reading verification — it will bash and ship in seconds
      - Finishes so fast it pattern-matches rather than reads; always gate explicitly
      - Skips edge cases unless forced to enumerate them first
      - Drifts from constraints mid-task on long sessions
      - Has a bash tool: verify with bash grep before trusting any output
      - Sandboxed remote environment — no internet in sandbox; web_search is a separate tool
    context_format: |
      Feed files as inline text with === FILE: path === separators.
      Never use file attachments — Grok reads inline text more reliably.
      Include soul.yml, rules.yml, voice.yml, and limits.yml first so constraints are in top-of-context.
      After pasting files, ask Grok to run: bash("grep -n 'def [function]' [file]")
      to prove it can locate code before it writes anything.
    reading_gate: |
      I am going to paste the full source of MASTER.
      Do not write any code yet. First, use your bash tool to run:

        grep -n "def " MASTER/lib/[module].rb | head -40

      Paste the output. Then answer ONLY these questions:
      1. What does [specific function] actually do, step by step?
      2. Where does the pipeline fail if a tool raises?
      3. What is the contract between [ModuleA] and [ModuleB]?
      4. List every place error handling is inconsistent.
      5. What are the 3 most structurally broken things?

      I will approve your reading before asking for any changes.
    output_format: |
      After gate approval, one fix at a time:
      "Fix #1 from your findings. Show:
       - Which files change
       - Exact diffs only (no prose wrapping)
       - What breaks downstream and why it won't
       Do NOT touch anything outside the scope of this fix."
    escalation: "Use 4.20 (2M context) for full-codebase work; 4.3 for single-file tasks."

  claude_sonnet:
    aliases: [claude-sonnet-4-6, anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-cli:claude-sonnet-4-6]
    context_window: "200K"
    strengths:
      - Multi-file refactoring with rule consistency
      - Enforces custom constraints (zsh discipline, style rules) reliably
      - Best time-to-correct-answer for architectural changes
      - Reads DEPLOY/OPERATOR.md and MASTER/data/*.yml as actual authority (/orient bootstrap for mental model)
      - Memory system (user/feedback/project/reference types) persists across sessions
      - Agent tool spawns parallel sub-agents; foreground vs background aware
      - Conversation history is stateful for safety checks — context carries forward
    traps:
      - Can over-explain; tell it to be terse upfront
      - May add unsolicited comments or docstrings — forbid explicitly
      - Asks confirmation questions; operator playbook auto-approve removes this
      - Uses ≤25 words between tool calls — keep prompts action-dense, not prose
      - Minimalist prose style by default; bullets only when structure genuinely aids
    context_format: |
      Claude bootstraps via /orient bootstrap and DEPLOY/OPERATOR.md. Feed additional context as:
      <file path="MASTER/lib/...">...</file> blocks or plain === FILE === separators.
      soul.yml, rules.yml, voice.yml, limits.yml, operator_principles.yml, skills_registry.yml,
      and project_context.yml are authoritative — reference them by name.
      Durable project context appends to data/project_context.yml via MemoryRecord.
      External agent memory (~/.claude/projects/.../memory/) persists across sessions when using Claude Code.
    reading_gate: |
      Read MASTER/data/soul.yml, rules.yml, voice.yml, limits.yml, and style.yml first.
      Then read [specific files].
      Before writing any code, state:
      - The invariant this change must not break
      - Which rules from rules.yml apply
      - Exact files touched
    output_format: |
      Terse. Active voice. Diffs only. No trailing summaries.
      Commit message in Strunk & White style on completion.
      Flag rule violations found during reading before fixing the task.
    escalation: "Escalate to opus for > 500-line rewrites or council decisions."

  claude_opus:
    aliases: [claude-opus-4-7, anthropic/claude-opus-4-7, claude-cli:claude-opus-4-7]
    context_window: "200K"
    strengths:
      - Architectural reasoning and trade-off analysis
      - Council/tribunal deliberation
      - Long multi-step refactors with dependency tracking
      - Constitutional / axiom reasoning
      - Extended thinking activates on ambiguous premises — self-corrects before answering
      - Mandatory web search before any present-day factual claim (built-in)
    traps:
      - Slow; do not use for quick fixes or single-file edits
      - May propose abstractions beyond scope — scope-cap explicitly
      - Cost: use only for tier1_critical or council tasks
      - Extended thinking is conditional on ambiguity — don't force it on routine tasks
      - Same model as Sonnet but behavior differs based on system prompt container structure
    context_format: |
      Same as claude_sonnet. Give it the full picture — it uses context well.
      Include previous council deliberations if continuing a thread.
      User preferences + project instructions containers alter behavior at runtime —
      structure your system prompt with explicit <project_instructions> blocks.
    reading_gate: |
      Before proposing any changes, produce a dependency graph of the modules
      affected and identify which axioms in axioms.jsonl would be violated
      by naive approaches.
    output_format: |
      Structured deliberation: finding → impact → options → recommendation.
      For code: diffs with explicit axiom-compliance notes.
    escalation: "This is the escalation target. For >0.90 quality threshold tasks only."

  gpt_4o:
    aliases: [gpt-4o, openai/gpt-4o, chatgpt, gpt-4.1, gpt-5]
    context_window: "128K"
    strengths:
      - Broad general knowledge, good at explaining unfamiliar APIs
      - Tool use and function calling reliability — most consistent structured output
      - bio tool persists key facts across sessions (but not code state)
      - canmore/canvas for iterative document and code editing
      - 'Agent mode: "go as far as you can without checking in" — useful for long agentic tasks'
    traps:
      - Confidently wrong on OpenBSD-specific details — always verify
      - Adds excessive prose; prepend "respond in code only, no prose" to suppress
      - Invents method names for Ruby gems it half-knows
      - Context degrades measurably above 80K — confirmed in its own system prompt
      - Personality-first by default; task-mode requires explicit framing
      - Agent mode treats screen-based instructions as potential prompt injection;
        requires explicit user confirmation before acting on them — design flows accordingly
      - Persona multiplexing (gpt-5.1): same model, different tones per system prompt variant
    context_format: |
      System prompt: include soul.yml content verbatim as constraints.
      Feed code as user messages with === FILE === separators.
      Keep total context under 80K to avoid degradation.
      Use canmore for iterative file editing if available — avoids full re-paste.
    reading_gate: |
      Before writing any code, list:
      - Every method in [file] that touches [concern]
      - The exact return type of [method]
      - Which callers would break if [method] changes signature
      Only proceed after I confirm your list is correct.
    output_format: |
      Code blocks with language tags. No markdown prose between diffs.
      End each response with: "Files changed: [list]"
    escalation: "Prefer DeepSeek for cost; use GPT-4o for tool-calling tasks. O3/O4-mini for hard logic."

  openai_o_series:
    aliases: [o3, o4-mini, openai/o3, openai/o4-mini]
    context_window: "200K"
    strengths:
      - Extended chain-of-thought reasoning with tunable effort (low/medium/high)
      - Best for hard logic, algorithmic bugs, multi-step planning
      - High reasoning effort = strongest math, proof, and correctness checks
    traps:
      - Cost scales steeply with reasoning effort tier; use low/medium for routine tasks
      - Does not benefit from "think step by step" — it already does; adding it wastes tokens
      - Slower than GPT-4o; do not use for mechanical edits or simple lookups
      - Like GPT-4o: screen instructions treated as potential injection in agentic mode
    context_format: |
      Minimal context — reasoning effort compensates for brevity.
      State the problem, the failing test or error, and the constraint.
      Set reasoning_effort: "high" only for correctness-critical or proof tasks.
    reading_gate: |
      State exactly what the code is supposed to do and what it actually does.
      Include the error output verbatim. Let reasoning run; do not interrupt.
    output_format: |
      Answer only; no reasoning exposition unless asked.
      Code blocks with language tags. One fix per response.
    escalation: "Use for logic bugs and correctness; route bulk edits to Sonnet or DeepSeek."

  deepseek_chat:
    aliases: [deepseek-chat, deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1, deepseek-v3]
    context_window: "64K"
    strengths:
      - Best cost/quality ratio for code tasks
      - Strong Ruby and Rails knowledge
      - Reliable at following explicit constraints
    traps:
      - Context window is tight; chunk aggressively (< 40K per call)
      - Less reliable on OpenBSD-specific tooling
      - Can produce subtly wrong diffs; always run a validation pass
    context_format: |
      Chunk into logical units: one module per call.
      Always include rules.yml summary as system prompt prefix.
      Keep each call focused: one concern, one module.
    reading_gate: |
      Summarize the responsibility of [module] in one sentence.
      List its public interface (method names + signatures only).
      Identify one thing that looks wrong before I give you the task.
    output_format: |
      Minimal diffs. No explanatory prose unless asked.
      Flag: "Rule violation found: [rule] at [file:line]" if any.
    escalation: "Escalate to deepseek_reasoner for multi-step logic or planning."

  deepseek_reasoner:
    aliases: [deepseek-reasoner, deepseek/deepseek-r1]
    context_window: "64K"
    strengths:
      - Chain-of-thought reasoning visible in <think> blocks
      - Best for logic bugs, algorithmic issues, planning
      - Finds non-obvious failure modes
    traps:
      - Very slow; do not use for mechanical edits
      - Reasoning tokens cost extra; scope questions tightly
      - May over-plan and under-produce; ask for plan + code together
    context_format: |
      Feed the minimal reproducing context only.
      Ask one well-scoped question: "Why does X fail when Y?"
      Include the actual error output.
    reading_gate: |
      Think through the execution path step by step before answering.
      Show your reasoning. Then give the fix.
    output_format: |
      Let <think> blocks run fully. Then extract the code from the final answer.
      Ignore prose in <think>; act on the conclusion only.
    escalation: "Use for council deliberation and hard bugs; not for bulk edits."

  kimi:
    aliases: [moonshot-v1, kimi, moonshotai/moonshot-v1-128k]
    context_window: "128K"
    strengths:
      - Very large effective context for Chinese + English mixed codebases
      - Strong at reading long documents and extracting structured info
      - Good at summarization and cross-file dependency mapping
    traps:
      - Weaker at Ruby than Python/Go; double-check gem APIs
      - Can produce overly literal translations of requirements
      - Less familiar with OpenBSD ecosystem
    context_format: |
      Feed the full codebase as a single blob — it handles long context well.
      Include MASTER/data/rules.yml inline as constraints header.
    reading_gate: |
      Read the full codebase. Then produce a dependency map:
      Module → files → public methods → callers.
      Do not write any code until the map is confirmed.
    output_format: |
      Structured: finding → affected files → proposed diff.
      One change per response.
    escalation: "Use for document analysis and cross-file mapping; code to DeepSeek."

  gemini_pro:
    aliases: [gemini-2.5-pro, google/gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-3-pro, google/gemini-3-pro, gemini-3.1-pro]
    context_window: "1M"
    strengths:
      - Largest reliable context window among readily available models
      - Good at whole-codebase analysis in one shot
      - Strong multimodal (can read screenshots of errors)
      - Structure-first response style — headings/tables/lists aid scanning
    traps:
      - Verbose by default; suppress with "respond concisely, code only"
      - Can hallucinate Ruby gem APIs confidently
      - Safety filters occasionally block legitimate code tasks
      - "Gemini API uses stateless python tool_code blocks — execution state does NOT
        persist between blocks. Variables from one block are gone in the next.
        Adapt injection template: each tool_code block must be self-contained."
      - "Personalization gating: 3-step check before using user data; may refuse
        to make inferences about the user even when benign"
      - Leaked system prompt is ~80% of actual instruction set; search result
        formatting and UX wording live in undocumented backend instructions
    context_format: |
      Feed entire MASTER codebase in one call — 1M context allows it.
      Include error logs and test output alongside source.
      Structure: [constraints] [source files] [task]
      Via API: wrap analysis in a single tool_code block; do not span state across blocks.
      Via AI Studio: plain text injection works; state persists within session.
    reading_gate: |
      Before any changes: identify the 5 highest-coupling points in the codebase.
      For each: name the files, the coupling type, and why it's a risk.
      Confirm before proceeding.
    output_format: |
      Respond with diffs only. Use unified diff format.
      End with: "Affected: [files]. Downstream risk: [yes/no + reason]."
    escalation: "Best for whole-repo analysis; route code writes to DeepSeek or Sonnet."

  mistral_large:
    aliases: [mistral-large, mistralai/mistral-large, le-chat]
    context_window: "128K"
    strengths:
      - Strong instruction following
      - Good at structured output (JSON, YAML)
      - Reliable for mechanical transformations
      - Active-voice, economy-of-language style baked into its system prompt
      - Le Chat: web_search + news_search + open_url available
    traps:
      - Less strong at architectural reasoning
      - Can miss implicit constraints; be explicit about every rule
      - news_search: avoid relative dates ("today"); always resolve to YYYY-MM-DD
    context_format: |
      Explicit system prompt with all constraints listed as numbered rules.
      Feed code in user messages with clear section headers.
    reading_gate: |
      List all constraints I just gave you, numbered, before writing any code.
    output_format: |
      Code blocks only. No prose. Confirm constraint compliance at end.
    escalation: "Use for structured data tasks; route architecture to stronger models."

# Universal rules that apply regardless of model:
universal:
  always_do:
    - Include soul.yml, rules.yml, voice.yml, limits.yml, and operator_principles.yml in every system prompt
    - Use /orient bootstrap for agent mental model — not deleted top-level .md stubs
    - Gate: verify reading before acting (model-specific gate above)
    - One fix at a time — never batch multiple concerns in one call
    - Ask for diffs, not full file rewrites (except on < 50-line files)
    - After any code output: ask "what breaks downstream?"
    - If model has a bash/code tool: use it to prove comprehension (grep for specific methods)
    - Calibrate context size to model: 80K GPT-4o, 40K DeepSeek, full-blast Grok/Gemini
  never_do:
    - Trust output on OpenBSD-specific commands without man page verification
    - Accept a response that finishes in < 5s for a > 200-line task
    - Skip the reading gate because "it's probably fine"
    - Let the model rename or restructure files without explicit approval
    - Accept invented method names without grepping the actual codebase
    - Assume Gemini API tool_code state persists between blocks — it does not
    - Force extended thinking on routine tasks — it triggers on ambiguity, not by volume
    - Trust a leaked system prompt as complete — ~80% of actual instructions are there;
      the rest lives in undocumented backend logic (search UX, result formatting, safety layers)
    - Send screen-sourced instructions to GPT/OpenAI agent without user confirmation gate
    - Invoke O3/O4-mini for mechanical edits — reasoning cost is wasted on non-logic tasks

  codebase_injection_template: |
    === CONSTRAINTS ===
    [paste soul.yml]
    [paste rules.yml key sections]

    === CODEBASE ===
    === FILE: MASTER/lib/now/cli.rb ===
    [content]
    === FILE: MASTER/lib/loop/sweep.rb ===
    [content]
    ... (continue for all relevant files)

    === TASK ===
    [specific ask]

    === READING GATE ===
    [model-specific gate from above]
```

### MASTER/data/llm_output_rules.yml

```yaml
# Runtime quality patterns loaded by Master::Judge::OutputCheck.
schema: 1

hallucination:
  - "i (?:created|added|wrote) `[^`]+\\.(?:rb|yml|md|js)`"
  - "(?:the command )?(?:produced|returned|output)(?:ed|s)? .{0,80}(?:as expected|successfully)"
  - "(?:the|this) `[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_:]+#\\w+` method (?:returns|provides|gives)"

refusal_failure:
  - "(?:i'?ll|i will|let me|sure,? i'?ll) (?:run|execute|apply|commit) .{0,80}(?<!done)$"
  - "(?:applying|running|committing) (?:the |this |that )?(?:patch|fix|change) now\\."

hedge_violation:
  - "\\b(?:will|would|could|might)\\s+(?:probably|possibly|likely|maybe)\\b"
  - "\\b(?:should|ought to)\\s+work\\b"

bias_surface:
  - "\\b(?:women|men|girls|boys) (?:naturally|typically|usually) (?:better|worse|more|less)"
  - "\\b(?:elderly|young people|millennials|boomers) (?:can'?t|don'?t|never|always)"

toxicity_surface:
  - "\\b(?:stupid|idiot|moron|retard|dumb)\\b.{0,40}(?:user|person|you)"
  - "(?:kill|hurt|attack) (?:yourself|themselves)"

refusal_failure_unhelpful:
  - "(?:i (?:cannot|can'?t)|sorry,? i (?:cannot|can'?t)) help with that\\.?$"
  - "as an ai language model"
```

### MASTER/data/load.yml

```yaml
# load.yml — Watcher thresholds.
# OS-level pressure that should make MASTER back off scans, defer autofix, or alert.
# Read by lib/loop/watcher.rb. Crossings publish system:warn / system:crit.

interval_seconds: 30

thresholds:
  load_avg_1m:
    warn: 2.0
    crit: 4.0

  mem_free_pct:      # lower = worse
    warn: 15.0
    crit: 5.0

  disk_root_pct:
    warn: 80
    crit: 95

  master_rss_mb:
    warn: 1024
    crit: 2048

# Back-off policy: heartbeat and fix_loop subscribe to system:warn/crit.
# - warn: skip the next idle scan cycle, log only.
# - crit: stop fix_loop background, defer autofix until system:sample shows ok.
policy:
  warn: skip_idle_scan
  crit: stop_fix_loop_background
```

```yaml
# Model routing profile — Grok primary (API or keyless browser), OpenRouter free fallback.

schema: 1
routing:
  enabled: true
  strategy: weighted
  escalation_enabled: true
  escalation_tier: strong
  provider: grok

weights: &weights
  quality: 0.50
  speed: 0.25
  cost: 0.25

fallback_policy:
  retries_per_tier: 1
  on:
    - timeout
    - network_error
    - refusal
    - insufficient_balance
    - rate_limit
    - quota_exceeded

failover:
  sequence: [fast, default, medium, strong]
  cooldown_seconds: 300
  max_retries: 2

defaults: &model_defaults
  score: { quality: 0.0, speed: 0.0, cost: 0.0 }
  context_window: 128000

model_defs:
  gemini_flash: &gemini_flash
    id: gemini-2.5-flash
    <<: *model_defaults
    score: { quality: 0.88, speed: 0.90, cost: 0.95 }
  gemini_pro: &gemini_pro
    id: gemini-2.5-pro
    <<: *model_defaults
    score: { quality: 0.95, speed: 0.70, cost: 0.80 }
  mistral_large: &mistral_large
    id: mistralai/mistral-large
    <<: *model_defaults
    score: { quality: 0.90, speed: 0.75, cost: 0.70 }
  mistral_small: &mistral_small
    id: mistralai/mistral-small-3.1-24b
    <<: *model_defaults
    score: { quality: 0.78, speed: 0.85, cost: 0.90 }
  deepseek_chat: &deepseek_chat
    id: deepseek-chat
    <<: *model_defaults
    context_window: 64000
    score: { quality: 0.96, speed: 0.85, cost: 0.95 }
  deepseek_reasoner: &deepseek_reasoner
    id: deepseek-reasoner
    <<: *model_defaults
    context_window: 64000
    score: { quality: 0.97, speed: 0.55, cost: 0.85 }
  deepseek_coder: &deepseek_coder
    id: deepseek-coder
    <<: *model_defaults
    context_window: 64000
    score: { quality: 0.85, speed: 0.70, cost: 0.95 }
  claude_sonnet: &claude_sonnet
    id: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6
    <<: *model_defaults
    context_window: 200000
    score: { quality: 0.95, speed: 0.75, cost: 0.60 }
  gemini_flash_openrouter: &gemini_flash_openrouter
    id: google/gemini-2.5-flash
    <<: *model_defaults

  file_write:       { min_quality: 0.88, preferred_tier: strong }
  autoloop:         { min_quality: 0.88, preferred_tier: strong }
  sweep:            { min_quality: 0.88, preferred_tier: strong }

  destructive:      { min_quality: 0.90, preferred_tier: strong }

continuity:

  updated_at: "2026-05-01T00:00:00Z"

openrouter:
  # When true, the router merges live :free slugs from the SQLite provider catalog
  # (populated by Providers::CatalogIndex#refresh). Read-only; no-ops until refreshed.
  use_live_catalog: true
  # Per-model daily cap before router skips the slug (OpenRouter free tier ~200/day/key).
  daily_quota_per_model: 200
  # Multiple keys rotate LRU to spread free-tier rate limits (20 req/min, 200/day each).
  keys_env:
    - OPENROUTER_API_KEY
    - OPENROUTER_API_KEY_2
    - OPENROUTER_API_KEY_3
  free_latest:
    - z-ai/glm-4.5-air:free
    - nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free
    - openai/gpt-oss-120b:free
    - qwen/qwen3-coder:free

    - deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free
    - meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free
    - meta-llama/llama-4-scout:free
    - google/gemma-2-9b-it:free

# Keyless free fallback via headless Chrome (ferrum gem). Auto-activates when no API keys
# are configured; opt-in anytime with MASTER_WEB_CHAT=1 or MASTER_KEYLESS=1.
# Selectors are best-effort — sites change often. Login cookies persist in the profile dir.
# Models use the web-chat: prefix. ToS-sensitive: never default when paid keys exist.
ferrum_web_chat:
  enabled_when_env: MASTER_WEB_CHAT
  auto_when_keyless: true
  profile_dir: "~/.config/master/web-chat-profile"
  free_latest:
    - web-chat:grok
    - web-chat:chatgpt
    - web-chat:kimi
    - web-chat:gemini
  providers:
    grok:
      url: https://grok.com/
      input_selector: "textarea, div[contenteditable='true'], div[role='textbox']"
      reply_selector: "div[class*='message'], article, div.markdown"
      timeout: 120
    chatgpt:
      url: https://chatgpt.com/
      input_selector: "div#prompt-textarea, textarea#prompt-textarea, div[contenteditable='true']"
      reply_selector: "div[data-message-author-role='assistant']"
      timeout: 120
    kimi:
      url: https://kimi.com/
      input_selector: "textarea, div[contenteditable='true'], div[role='textbox']"
      reply_selector: "div.markdown-body, div[class*='assistant'], div[class*='message']"
      timeout: 120
    gemini:
      url: https://gemini.google.com/app
      input_selector: "div.ql-editor[contenteditable='true'], div[contenteditable='true']"
      reply_selector: "message-content, div[class*='response']"
      timeout: 120

# Provider trust tracked over time; weights routing beyond raw cost.
# Source: master.json v225 reunification (#52).
trust_scoring:
  initial_score:        0.50
  success_increment:    0.02
  failure_decrement:    0.10
  deprecate_below:      0.20
  persist_to:           "data/provider_trust.yml"
  consider_in_routing:  true

three_mirror_redundancy:
  # Three models vote; ship only on >= 2 agreement for critical fixes.
  # Source: cross-cutting reunification (#95).
  enabled_for:   [tier1_critical, security_relevant, irreversible]
  pool:          ["anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6", "z-ai/glm-4.5-air:free", "moonshotai/kimi-k2"]
  quorum:        2
  on_disagreement: "fall back to council vote with all dissent recorded"

# Tier-D (local ollama) — env-gated; activates only when OLLAMA_BASE_URL is set.
# Default: http://localhost:11434/v1 (OpenAI-compatible endpoint).
# Trust starts at 0.40 (below cloud providers) until measured success raises it.
ollama:
  enabled_when_env: OLLAMA_BASE_URL
  default_base_url: "http://localhost:11434/v1"
  initial_trust: 0.40
  use_for: [exploration, fallback_default]   # cheapest-acceptable tasks only
  never_for: [council, sweep, autoloop, file_write, destructive]

# Replicate media slugs — image/video/TTS; routed via Repligen, VideoChain, Voice::Engines.
media_providers:
  replicate:
    env: [REPLICATE_API_TOKEN, REPLICATE_API_KEY]
    image_default: black-forest-labs/flux-1.1-pro
    image_flagship: black-forest-labs/flux-2-pro
    tts_default: jaaari/kokoro-82m
    video_default: kwaivgi/kling-v2.1
```

### MASTER/data/openbsd.yml

```yaml
# openbsd.yml — OpenBSD config validators
# Restored from master.yml v49.75; extended for OpenBSD 7.8

man_base_url: "https://man.openbsd.org"
cache_ttl: 86400

configs:
  pf.conf:
    daemon: pf
    man: pf.conf.5
    required_patterns:
      - "set skip on lo"
    warnings:
      - pattern: "pass all"
        message: "Overly permissive — add interface/protocol guards"

  nsd.conf:
    daemon: nsd
    man: nsd.conf.5
    required_patterns:
      - "server:"
      - "zone:"
    warnings:
      - pattern: "rrl-size"
        absent_message: "Missing RRL config — vulnerable to amplification DDoS"
      - pattern: "hide-version"
        absent_message: "Consider hide-version: yes"

  httpd.conf:
    daemon: httpd
    man: httpd.conf.5
    required_patterns:
      - "server"

  smtpd.conf:
    daemon: smtpd
    man: smtpd.conf.5
    required_patterns:
      - "listen on"
      - "action"
      - "match"
    warnings:
      - pattern: "match from any"
        message: "Open relay risk — restrict to authenticated senders"

  relayd.conf:
    daemon: relayd
    man: relayd.conf.5
    required_patterns:
      - "relay"

  acme-client.conf:
    daemon: acme-client
    man: acme-client.conf.5
    required_patterns:
      - "authority"
      - "domain"

  doas.conf:
    daemon: doas
    man: doas.conf.5
    required_patterns:
      - "permit"
    warnings:
      - pattern: "nopass"
        message: "Allows passwordless privilege escalation"

  sshd_config:
    daemon: sshd
    man: sshd_config.5
    warnings:
      - pattern: "PermitRootLogin yes"
        message: "Security risk — use PermitRootLogin prohibit-password"
      - pattern: "PasswordAuthentication yes"
        message: "Consider key-only auth"

  ntpd.conf:
    daemon: ntpd
    man: ntpd.conf.5
    required_patterns:
      - "server"

  unbound.conf:
    daemon: unbound
    man: unbound.conf.5
    required_patterns:
      - "server:"


system_health_checks:
  - name: "patch_level"
    command: "syspatch -c"
    expected: ""
  - name: "disk_usage"
    command: "df -h /"
    max_percent: 80

service_definitions:
  master:
    service: "master"
    check: "rcctl check master"
    restart: "doas rcctl restart master"
    logs: "/var/log/master.log"
```

### MASTER/data/operator_playbook.yml

```yaml
# Operator playbook — durable lessons from production sessions.
# Loaded at startup (limits.yml) and via Ground::OperatorPlaybook.
# Each lesson: signal → action → proof. Prefer executable proof over TODO checkboxes.

version: 1
updated: "2026-06-25"

lessons:
  - id: relayd_master_health_up
    area: openbsd
    signal: "relayd marks master:53187 empty; HTTPS curl empty reply while local /up works"
    action: "relayd.conf must check http \"/up\" for master (not \"/\" — face boot is slow). rc.d/master waits up to 30s for /up then rcctl restart relayd."
    proof: "relayctl show hosts → master active; curl -fsS https://ai.brgen.no/up"

  - id: relayd_after_master_restart
    area: openbsd
    signal: "doas rcctl restart master leaves ai.brgen.no empty until manual relayd restart"
    action: "Use tracked DEPLOY/openbsd/etc/rc.d/master (wait-for-/up + relayd restart). Post-reboot run doas rcctl restart master once."
    proof: "rc.d/master contains wait loop on PORT/up and rcctl restart relayd"

  - id: relayd_stale_backend_tables
    area: openbsd
    signal: "relayctl show hosts marks backend empty/down while curl http://127.0.0.1:PORT/up returns 200; HTTPS empty reply"
    action: "doas rcctl restart relayd after mass app restarts. Cron runs /usr/local/bin/relayd-watchdog every 5 min to auto-heal stale tables."
    proof: "relayctl show hosts → all tables active; ruby34 DEPLOY/openbsd/health_check.rb"

  - id: resource_guard_shedding
    area: openbsd
    signal: "Rails apps stopped after cron; only master/brgen remain"
    action: "Create /var/db/pub4_all_apps or run DEPLOY/openbsd/start_all_apps.sh to pin all services against resource_guard.sh shedding."
    proof: "test -f /var/db/pub4_all_apps; doas rcctl check brgen amber bsdports hjerterom"

  - id: rails_phantom_foreign_keys
    area: rails
    signal: "SQLite no such table main.listings|buyers|likers|orders|menu_items during seed or insert"
    action: "Never use foreign_key: true alone on namespaced refs — use foreign_key: { to_table: :users } or :marketplace_listings. Run DEPLOY/rails/check_phantom_foreign_keys.rb."
    proof: "ruby DEPLOY/rails/check_phantom_foreign_keys.rb exits 0"

  - id: rails_model_schema_drift
    area: rails
    signal: "unknown attribute, MissingAttributeError actor_id, strict_loading violations in seeds"
    action: "Align models to schema.rb before seeds; grep belongs_to vs create_table; guard optional columns with has_attribute?; query associations instead of lazy-loading under strict_loading."
    proof: "RAILS_ENV=test bundle exec rails db:seed exits 0 as app user"

  - id: rails_shared_concern_dupes
    area: rails
    signal: "no such column taggings.post_id — polymorphic taggable expected"
    action: "Do not redeclare has_many from Shared concerns (Taggable, Votable, Reactable) on host models."
    proof: "Post model includes Shared::Taggable only once"

  - id: rails_up_vs_root
    area: rails
    signal: "bin/ci passes /up but production landing 500; Could not find table cities"
    action: "Treat /up as liveness only. Run db:migrate on production; ensure locality tables exist (EnsureLocalityTables); DomainRegistry must guard table_exists?(:cities); seed CitySeed.sync! after migrate."
    proof: "curl -fsSI https://brgen.no/ returns 200; sqlite3 db/production.sqlite3 '.tables' lists cities"

  - id: vps_ci_app_user
    area: deploy
    signal: "bin/ci fails as dev user; bundle without errors"
    action: "Run CI as app user: doas sh -c \"su -m brgen -c 'cd /home/brgen/app && bin/ci'\". One app at a time on 1 GiB VM."
    proof: "su -m brgen -c bin/ci per app"

  - id: master_smoke_low_resource
    area: master
    signal: "bin/smoke pipe command times out on 1 GiB VPS"
    action: "MASTER_LOW_RESOURCE=1 or MASTER_SMOKE_PIPE_TIMEOUT=90 for smoke/probe on vm23."
    proof: "MASTER_LOW_RESOURCE=1 bundle34 exec ruby bin/smoke --web"

  - id: master_web_osman_defaults
    area: master_web
    signal: "White page, silent TTS, or Osman blocked after voice/lang regressions"
    action: "Defaults live in speech.rb (:osman), face.part4 TTS_DEFAULT_VOICE, chat voice-picker HTML, guardVoice (no ms-lang block on osman). rc.d/master warms TtsSupervisor after /up. Assets are fingerprinted under /assets/face-*.js."
    proof: "curl page includes voice-picker osman; GET /chat/tts?voice=osman returns audio; test -S /home/dev/pub4/MASTER/.master/tts.sock; bin/smoke --web clean"

  - id: ecology_layer_visibility
    area: master_web
    signal: "SSE events fire but ecology trails/weather invisible"
    action: "Ecology canvas must sit above #face (z-index 2, mix-blend-mode screen). cognition_ecology.js listens on master:visual; render loop restarts on visibility + visual events."
    proof: "grep 'z-index: 2' MASTER/web/public/face.css; browser devtools shows #cognition-ecology above canvas#face"

  - id: ship_proof_not_checkboxes
    area: process
    signal: "Backlog marked done but production gaps remain"
    action: "Ship readiness requires bin/probe repo, per-app bin/ci, health_check.rb, and db:seed — not checkbox files. Fix executable failures only."
    proof: "bin/probe deploy; ruby DEPLOY/openbsd/health_check.rb on VPS"

  - id: post_sync_vps_proof
    area: deploy
    signal: "Code pushed but services stale or untested on vm23"
    action: "After git pull: SKIP_MASTER_SCAN=1 zsh DEPLOY/openbsd/sh/vps_on_vm_install.sh; doas rcctl restart master; bundle34 exec bin/ci per app; bundle34 exec bin/smoke in MASTER; ruby34 DEPLOY/openbsd/health_check.rb; curl https://ai.brgen.no/up"
    proof: "doas rcctl check master brgen amber bsdports hjerterom; browser smoke on ai.brgen.no face"

  - id: rails_rcd_canonical_names
    area: openbsd
    signal: "rcctl stop brgen_rails kills brgen on same port; duplicate rc.d scripts"
    action: "Canonical rc.d names are bare app names (brgen, amber, …). Never rcctl stop *_rails. retire_legacy_rails_rcd in deploy scripts removes stale /etc/rc.d/*_rails."
    proof: "ls DEPLOY/openbsd/etc/rc.d/ shows brgen not brgen_rails; grep -r '_rails' DEPLOY/openbsd returns empty"

  - id: master_scan_bundle_exec
    area: deploy
    signal: "openbsd.sh --sync-configs aborts: cannot load such file -- zeitwerk"
    action: "MASTER bin/cli must run as dev via bundle34 exec (openbsd.sh uses su dev, not su -m — -m keeps HOME=/root). Set MASTER_SCAN_ONLY=1 MASTER_SAFE_MODE=1."
    proof: "su dev -c 'cd MASTER && MASTER_SCAN_ONLY=1 bundle34 exec ruby bin/cli /scan DEPLOY --depth deep' exits 0"

  - id: relayd_csp_overwrites_rails
    area: master_web
    signal: "https://ai.brgen.no shows black screen; curl :53187 has script-src nonce but HTTPS CSP lacks nonce"
    action: "Do not set Content-Security-Policy in relayd.conf — it replaces Rails headers and breaks nonce-gated inline boot scripts. Keep HSTS and other hardening headers in relayd; let each app own CSP."
    proof: "curl -sI https://ai.brgen.no/ | grep -i content-security shows Rails policy with script-src nonce"

  - id: sass_embedded_npm_cache
    area: rails
    signal: "bundle34 install fails on sass-embedded; npm EACCES on /root/.npm when installing as app user via doas"
    action: "pkg_add node if missing. When running bundle install via doas su -m <app>, export HOME=/home/<app> and NPM_CONFIG_CACHE=/home/<app>/.npm so npm does not touch root-owned cache."
    proof: "su -m brgen -c 'cd /home/brgen/app && bundle34 check' exits 0; bin/rails dartsass:build succeeds"

  - id: takeaway_seed_city_association
    area: rails
    signal: "db:seed:replant fails after Playlist with City expected, got String"
    action: "CityTenantable adds belongs_to :city on takeaway_restaurants, colliding with the legacy string city column. Set ActsAsTenant.current_tenant in seeds.rb; omit city: from create! and use update_column(:city, label) for the display string."
    proof: "RAILS_ENV=test bundle exec rails db:seed:replant exits 0 in brgen"

  - id: live_search_empty_query_count
    area: rails
    signal: "live_search_test fails on empty query .none scope count"
    action: "Shared::LiveSearch#safe_count returns 0 when query.blank? before calling null_relation? or count on arbitrary scopes."
    proof: "bundle exec rails test test/services/live_search_test.rb in brgen"

  - id: github_actions_billing_lock
    area: ci
    signal: "MASTER Tests workflow fails in ~5s with no job logs; email on every push"
    action: "GitHub account billing lock blocks runners. Pause push/pull_request triggers (workflow_dispatch only) until billing fixed at github.com/settings/billing. Re-enable .github/workflows/master-tests.yml and master-through-master.yml triggers after."
    proof: "gh workflow list shows paused; push does not enqueue Actions email"

  - id: gh_auth_vps_and_workstation
    area: deploy
    signal: "gh api returns HTTP 401 on VPS or Mac; cannot inspect PRs/workflows remotely"
    action: "Run gh auth login on each host that needs GitHub API. VPS: su dev -c 'gh auth login'. Never commit tokens."
    proof: "gh auth status shows logged in; gh api user returns 200"

  - id: pf_ssh_not_bruteforce
    area: openbsd
    signal: "Operator assumes SSH lockout is pf bruteforce after rapid reconnects"
    action: "Tracked pf.conf exempts SSH (pass in quick … port 22) before bruteforce table. Bruteforce is fed by HTTP/HTTPS rate limits only. Lockouts are usually RAM/CPU saturation from parallel SSH or bin/ci — use tmux, one app CI at a time, flush bruteforce only when HTTP wedge suspected."
    proof: "grep 'port 22' DEPLOY/openbsd/etc/pf.conf shows quick pass before block quick from <bruteforce>"

  - id: vps_one_ssh_no_parallel_ci
    area: deploy
    signal: "load averages >10 on vm23; dozens of ruby in D state; rcctl master/amber failed; SSH hangs"
    action: "Never open parallel SSH sessions to vm23. Use zsh DEPLOY/openbsd/sh/vps_ci.sh APP (mutex via /var/tmp/pub4-ci.lock) or vps_ci_all.sh for serial six-app proof. MASTER scan: zsh DEPLOY/openbsd/sh/vps_master_scan.sh. resource_guard cron runs stale_ci_cleanup.ksh when load>=4. Kill stale local ssh clients first; doas rcctl restart master amber after cleanup. If D-state ruby won't die: host console vmctl stop/start vm23."
    proof: "uptime load <4; test -f /var/tmp/pub4-ci.lock; zsh DEPLOY/openbsd/sh/vps_ci.sh brgen; doas rcctl check master brgen amber"

  - id: vps_ci_shared_tree_path
    area: deploy
    signal: "Importmap/RuboCop still run on VPS despite ci.rb fix; postpro resolves to /home/postpro"
    action: "config/ci.rb requires ../../shared from app/config → /home/<app>/shared (not /home/<app>/app/shared). vps_ci.sh syncs full DEPLOY/rails/shared there plus code overlay. Set PUB4_RAILS_ROOT=/home/dev/pub4/DEPLOY/rails for DeployPaths. Postpro/repligen: Pub4::DeployPaths or MASTER/tools/*.rb — never Rails.root/../../postpro alone on copy-tree."
    proof: "grep unless vps_host /home/brgen/shared/config/ci.rb; ruby -e 'require \"pub4/deploy_paths\"' under brgen app finds /home/dev/pub4/MASTER/tools/postpro.rb"

  - id: vps_ci_lock_perms
    area: deploy
    signal: "pub4-ci-guard: EACCES on flock or EPERM deleting lock.holder"
    action: "Lock at /var/tmp/pub4-ci.lock mode 666 (vps_ci ensure_ci_lock). Do not pre-create .holder as root — vps_ci removes stale holder before CI. CiGuard swallows EPERM on holder delete."
    proof: "ls -l /var/tmp/pub4-ci.lock; zsh DEPLOY/openbsd/sh/vps_ci.sh brgen exits 0"
```

### MASTER/data/operator_principles.yml

```yaml
---
meta:
  source: runtime authority — edit operator_principles.yml directly; never add data/principles/*.md
  count: 27
  order: importance — workflow, verification, architecture, code craft, presentation, git, voice
  resolves: soul.yml aesthetic_rules and style.yml line_order defer here for operator intent; scan rules in rules/unit.yml
principles:
- id: feedback_operator_autonomy
  name: "Operator Autonomy — decisive execution without permission loops"
  description: Scan→sweep without ask; one approval runs the backlog; short directives bind; pause only for destructive or ambiguous forks
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    When scan finds violations, sweep to convergence immediately—never pause for fix confirmation. One approved direction runs the entire backlog without per-step want-me-to prompts. Ship all, yes, do it, and kill X keep Y are binding orders. Ask only before destructive shared-state edits, material ambiguity, or genuine either-or forks.
- id: feedback_execute_not_instruct
  name: "Fail Fast — execute, never instruct"
  description: Run probes, gates, tests, and fixes in this environment; command output is the definition of done
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    Run probes, gates, tests, and fixes yourself. Never end with you should run X when X is executable here. Gate stdout and test output beat narrative completion. On failure, diagnose and retry—do not hand the chore to the operator. Aligns with soul FAIL_VISIBLY and rules/unit.yml FAIL_VISIBLY.
- id: feedback_scan_sweep_convergence
  name: "Fixed Point — deep scan then sweep to convergence"
  description: Run through MASTER means deep scan plus sweep; standing orders handle post-write lint and drift
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    Run through MASTER means deep scan on the path, then sweep until clean or blocked. Standing orders lint written paths and audit lib/ for constitution drift after mutations. Use plain language—check my edits, fix path—not memorized /scan /fix chains. Soul DEEP_SCAN_ONLY forbids quick or standard scan depths.
- id: feedback_council_when_risky
  name: "Deliberative Review — council only when risky"
  description: Six-persona Review-stage council with Security veto on dangerous diffs—not every single-file fix
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    Council is Review-stage deliberation with Security veto—the operator says tribunal, the code says council. Run it on dangerous patterns, multi-file diffs, or when config enables council. Scan plus sweep is the default loop; council is conditional, not automatic.
- id: feedback_probe_before_ship
  name: "Verify Before Ship — integrity gates block done"
  description: DEPLOY or web edits require integrity or crawl probes; gate failure keeps the task open
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    After DEPLOY/ or MASTER/web/ edits, run bin/probe integrity or ruby DEPLOY/integrity_gate.rb before declaring done. HTTP crawl syncs apps.yml to master.json. On VPS use MASTER_CRAWL_BROWSER=1 when primer, face-session, or ping/pong matter. Gate failure means the task is still open.
- id: feedback_vps_serial_truth
  name: "Single Source of Truth — VPS serial production verify"
  description: One SSH session, verify on dev@46.23.89.226, copy openbsd edits back to git same session
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    One SSH session—no parallel bin/ci. Production truth is dev@46.23.89.226. macOS may edit locally and HTTP-probe; Ferrum face crawl defaults to VPS unless MASTER_CRAWL_BROWSER=1. Copy any DEPLOY/openbsd/ VPS edit back to git in the same session. Use tmux for long deploys.
- id: feedback_restart_rails
  name: "No Hot Reload — restart master per web deploy"
  description: Falcon does not reload; one file one doas rcctl restart master; wait before curl
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    After each MASTER/web/, live lib/, or data YAML deploy on VPS, run doas rcctl restart master—one file, one restart. Wait about two seconds before curl. CLI-only local edits skip restart. Never batch web edits and restart once at the end.
- id: feedback_device_limits
  name: "Offload Compute — VPS not device"
  description: Builds, bundle, git, and CI on VPS; device is lightweight fallback only
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    Default edits, bundle, git, clones, and builds to the VPS. Termux or Android only when SSH is down. macOS is for local edit plus HTTP probe—not CPU-heavy CI. Ferrum browser tests belong on VPS or when explicitly forced.
- id: feedback_configuration_as_code
  name: "Configuration as Code — YAML authority and living stubs"
  description: Runtime truth in YAML and /orient; stub READMEs track surface changes only
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    Runtime-read material lives in operator_principles.yml, skills_registry.yml, project_context.yml, and Ground::BootstrapDocs (/orient). Allowed data markdown only SOUL.md, CANON.md, IDENTITY.md, skills/README.md. Top-level README files are one-paragraph stubs pointing at runtime truth—not prose duplication. When commands or behavior change, refresh stubs in the same or next commit without being asked.
- id: feedback_flat_hierarchy
  name: "Flat Hierarchy — aggressive merge and rename"
  description: OpenBSD-flat layout; paths named like dense Rails parameterize slugs—Strunk-clean snake_case
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    After every mutation, aggressively merge thin siblings and rename misfit paths before creating files. Name every path like a Rails parameterize slug at max information density: lowercase snake_case (Ruby paths, not URL hyphens), each underscore token a concrete noun or verb, Strunk omit needless words—no main, misc, util, helper, handler, or abbreviation filler. crawl_browser and domain_alignment_gate are good; misc_util, cbp, and foo_helper are not. Target OpenBSD-flat layout, Zeitwerk truth (path equals constant), Roda-tight trees. Fold *_support into parents; extend integrity_gate, crawl_support, browser_probe_support, or bin/probe CHECKS instead of new scripts; lib/ depth ≤4 unless the domain warrants more. Standing order aggressive_merge flags low-density slugs on every write—default merge or rename unless council blocks.
- id: feedback_merge_before_multiply
  name: "DRY — one expression per idea in code"
  description: Extract or parameterize duplicated logic; singularity wins for YAML data
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    Before copying a block to vary one literal, extract or parameterize. Scan enforces via rules/unit.yml DRY; limits.yml singularity wins for YAML data. File and module sprawl is Flat Hierarchy—not a second copy of the same gate script.
- id: feedback_no_new_files
  name: "YAGNI — edit in place, no new files without approval"
  description: Patch originals; Flat Hierarchy merge/rename runs before any new path
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    Edit the original path—no _fixed.rb, staging copies, or new files without approval. Try Flat Hierarchy merge/rename first on every touch. Transient /tmp/patch.rb on VPS is fine for in-place runs. Do not add config tiers that only weaken quality. Scan enforces via rules/unit.yml speculative-generality rules.
- id: feedback_importance_order
  name: "Inverted Pyramid — importance-ordered file lines"
  description: Public API and main flow in the top third; helpers and constants last
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    Every touched file flows high-to-low importance: requires, declaration, public API, core algorithm, private helpers, constants, edge cases. Applies to ruby, yaml, erb, js, css, html, sh, md. Soul IMPORTANCE_ORDER and style.yml line_order are the machine sequence; INVERTED_PYRAMID (same name, prose/commits/logs) means lead with the fact—context trails.
- id: feedback_style
  name: "KISS — minimal correct code"
  description: Shortest form that preserves behavior; no filler, ceremony, or defensive noise
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    Write the shortest correct form in every language—no filler, redundant branches, or ceremonial patterns. No defensive over-engineering or comments that restate code. Scan enforces via rules/unit.yml KISS and soul SIMPLEST_WORKS. Distinct from Craft (proactive polish beyond scope) and Boy Scout Rule (full-file lint on touch).
- id: feedback_strunk_white
  name: "Strunk & White — active prose and casing"
  description: Active voice, sentence case, no ASCII banners; commits imperative ≤72 chars
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    Active voice, omit needless words, concrete nouns and verbs, one idea per sentence. Sentence case in prose, comments, logs, and CLI; snake_case in code; capitalize commit subjects. No equals banners or bracket tags—use ok: and warn: prefixes. Soul STRUNK_ACTIVE and NO_ASCII_DECORATION enforce this in scan.
- id: feedback_lint_beautify
  name: "Boy Scout Rule — full-file lint and comment hygiene on touch"
  description: Lint and beautify the whole file; delete stale comments; keep one-line WHY only
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    Touching a file obligates a full-file lint and beautify pass—not only edited lines. Collapse double blanks, fix spacing, verify syntax. Reassess every comment: delete what-comments and banners; keep one-line WHY only when non-obvious. style.yml comments.reassess_on_touch and sweep RECOMMENT enforce this; soul NO_CONSECUTIVE_BLANK_LINES caps blank lines.
- id: feedback_shell_discipline
  name: "OpenBSD Shell Discipline — Ruby and zsh, not GNU text tools"
  description: Agent session and repo scripts ban sed, awk, grep pipes, python; use Ruby and doas
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    Ban sed, awk, grep, head, tail, find, wc, sudo, perl, and python in agent shell calls and committed scripts—BSD sed breaks GNU idioms. Use Ruby read/write, Grep and Glob tools, doas, zsh builtins. No pipe chains when a single Ruby or tool call suffices. git, bundle, and ssh stay allowed.
- id: feedback_html_css_style
  name: "Semantic HTML — structure over class soup"
  description: Bare element selectors; Rails tag helpers; no divitis or utility-class strings
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    Prefer bare selectors—nav a, main, h1—over nav-link or container class soup. Use Rails tag helpers over content_tag; omit class attributes unless brand, btn, or badge semantics require them. Structure and tags carry meaning; classes are a last resort.
- id: feedback_flat_pixels
  name: "Flat Design — uniform pixels unless collective 3D"
  description: No fake depth, z-scale, or parallax; exception when pixels resemble a 3D model
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    UI and particles stay flat two-dimensional—uniform size and alpha, no fake depth or parallax. Exception: pixels collectively resemble a three-dimensional model such as face mode. Soul FLAT_UI enforces the same rule in scan.
- id: feedback_motion_color_grading
  name: "Motion Design — eased transitions and cinema palette"
  description: Cubic easing and shadow-midtone-highlight triplets; no linear snap or raw primaries
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    Ease all motion with frame-independent delta time—ease-out arrivals, ease-in-out crossfades, never linear snap. Palettes use complementary anchors and shadow-midtone-highlight triplets with roughly six-hundred-millisecond lerps. Soul CINEMA_PALETTE enforces the same rule in scan.
- id: feedback_git_commits
  name: "Atomic Commits — frequent, one concern each"
  description: Commit after meaningful change; trust autocommit standing order; Strunk messages
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    Commit after every meaningful change—do not batch unrelated work. Standing order autocommit_post_chat handles post-mutation turns; avoid duplicate hand commits unless splitting logical units. One concern per commit when practical; Strunk-style imperative messages.
- id: feedback_diverged_branch_sync
  name: "Cherry-Pick — diverged main onto origin tip"
  description: Tag backup, reset to origin/main, cherry-pick intended commits; no force-push main
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    When push rejects diverged main with overlapping commits, tag backup-pre-sync-YYYY-MM-DD, reset hard to origin/main, cherry-pick only intended commits, resolve conflicts, push. Prefer cherry-pick over rebasing mixed history. Never force-push main.
- id: feedback_universal_cross_disciplinary_rules
  name: "Gestalt — one principle, many media adapters"
  description: SMALL_PARTS and kin apply to Ruby, HTML, CSS, and prose via rules.yml adapters
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    MASTER rules express medium-agnostic principles with per-language adapters in rules.yml. SMALL_PARTS, vertical rhythm, nesting depth, and naming silhouette are the same law in Ruby, markup, and prose—only the detector changes. Design, structure, and copy are one discipline.
- id: feedback_meta_framing
  name: "Systems Thinking — meta questions over diff dumps"
  description: End batches with shape questions; ranked options with payoff and risk
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    After a batch, surface what is missing or structurally off—not an itemized diff dump. End with one consolidation question. Are we missing X gets five to eight ranked options with payoff and risk. Land all means batch and commit without per-item reconfirmation.
- id: feedback_micro_refinements
  name: "Craft — micro-refinements without being asked"
  description: Tighter words, honest names, spacing fixes adjacent to the task
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    Notice and fix micro-refinements—tighter words, honest names, correct spacing, better glyphs—even beyond the stated task. Apply without asking; mention only non-obvious changes. Complements KISS (minimal scope) and Boy Scout Rule (lint on touch)—this is proactive polish when you see it.
- id: feedback_master_prompt_aesthetic
  name: "Prompt Lock — oh-my-zsh MASTER line is canonical"
  description: bold-red master, dim metadata, dollar terminator; ornament elsewhere
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    Keep Master::Renderer prompt_line unchanged: bold-red master, dim branch and phase, dim token bar, dollar terminator. Do not simplify or recolor it. New ornamentation belongs in reply tags, status rows, or dmesg—not the prompt line.
- id: feedback_voice_terse_unix
  name: "Unix Philosophy — terse, composable, perfectionist voice"
  description: One job per unit; silence on success; cut filler in MASTER and agent output
  type: feedback
  body: |-
    Voice is terse and unix-like: one job per unit, silence on success, composable lines, no corporate filler. Perfectionism means zero violations and fixed-point convergence. Operator replies use plain English with proper casing; kernel and dmesg stay lowercase terse.
```
